{{Short description|American oceanographer (1944–2019)}}
[[File:Harvard Professor James McCarthy.jpg|thumb|Professor James McCarthy en route to the North Pole]]
'''James J. McCarthy''' (January 25, 1944 – December 11, 2019)<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://environment.harvard.edu/remembering-jim-mccarthy|title=Remembering Jim McCarthy, 1944–2019|last=lhanrahan|date=2019-12-12|website=Harvard University Center for the Environment|language=en|access-date=2019-12-13|archive-date=2019-12-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191212222725/http://environment.harvard.edu/remembering-jim-mccarthy|url-status=dead}}</ref> was a Professor of [[Biological Oceanography]] at [[Harvard]] and was president of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] from February 2008 to February 2009.<ref name="starting-date">{{cite web | url=http://www.aaas.org/news/releases/2008/0407mccarthy.shtml | title=AAAS President James J. McCarthy: Scientists Should Share the "Wow" Factor in Their Work | access-date=April 7, 2011 | author=Ham, Becky | date=April 7, 2008 | archive-date=April 20, 2011 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110420002656/http://www.aaas.org/news/releases/2008/0407mccarthy.shtml | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="ending-date">{{cite web | url=http://www.aaas.org/news/releases/2009/0129aaas_elex.shtml | title=Alice S. Huang Chosen To Serve As AAAS President-Elect | access-date=April 7, 2011 | date=January 29, 2009 | archive-date=April 21, 2011 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110421170008/http://www.aaas.org/news/releases/2009/0129aaas_elex.shtml | url-status=dead }}</ref>

McCarthy was the Alexander Agassiz Professor of Biological Oceanography in the Department of Organismic and Evolutionary Biology and former Master of [[Pforzheimer House]]. He was also Acting Curator of the Malacology Department in the Museum of Comparative Zoology.

His studies addressed factors that regulate the processes of primary production and nutrient supply in upper ocean, approached using controlled laboratory studies and field investigations. Study sites ranged from near shore to the open ocean. Later field research sites included the North Atlantic, equatorial Pacific, and Arabian Sea.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.oeb.harvard.edu/faculty/mccarthy/mccarthy-oeb.html|title=Harvard website}}</ref>

He was on the faculty of the [[Harvard Medical School Center for Health and the Global Environment]].<ref>
{{cite journal|last=Russell|first=Christine|date=January 2009|title=First Wave|journal=Science News|volume=175|issue=1|pages=25–29|doi=10.1002/scin.2009.5591750125}}<!--|access-date=2009-03-29 --></ref>

==Biography==
McCarthy grew up in [[Sweet Home, Oregon]] and graduated from Sweet Home High School in 1962.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://archive.boston.com/news/science/articles/2008/04/07/a_witness_to_global_warming/|title=A witness to global warming|author=Baker, Billy |work=[[Boston Globe]] |date=April 7, 2008 |access-date=March 14, 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.sweethomenews.com/story/2018/03/14/news/shhs-alum-harvard-prof-wins-nobel-prize-for-the-environment/20366.html|title=SHHS alum, Harvard prof, wins 'Nobel Prize for the Environment'|author=Morgan, Sean |work=[[Sweet Home New Era]] |date=March 14, 2018 |access-date=March 14, 2018 }}</ref>

McCarthy received his undergraduate degree in biology from [[Gonzaga University]], and his Ph.D. from [[Scripps Institution of Oceanography]] in 1971.  His research interests related to the regulation of [[plankton]] productivity in the sea, and in later years focused on regions that are strongly affected by seasonal and inter-annual variation in climate.

From 1979 until 2002 McCarthy was the Director of Harvard University's [[Museum of Comparative Zoology]]. He held faculty appointments in the Department of Organismic and Evolutionary Biology and the Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences, and he was the Head Tutor for degrees in Environmental Science and Public Policy.

From 1986 to 1993, he chaired the international committee that establishes research priorities and oversees implementation of the [[International Geosphere-Biosphere Programme]].  He was the founding editor for the [[American Geophysical Union]]'s journal ''Global Biogeochemical Cycles''.  He was involved in two of the recent international assessments on climate impacts. He served as co-chair of the [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change|IPCC]], Working Group II, which had responsibilities for assessing impacts of and vulnerabilities to global climate change for the Third IPCC Assessment (2001).  He was also one of the lead authors on the recently completed Arctic Climate Impact Assessment.

McCarthy was also a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], and a Foreign Member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://chge.med.harvard.edu/about/faculty/mccarthy.html |title=CHGE Website |access-date=2009-02-25 |archive-date=2005-12-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051230160641/http://chge.med.harvard.edu/about/faculty/mccarthy.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He was emeritus chair of the Board of Directors for the [[Union of Concerned Scientists]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ucsusa.org/about/people/james-j-mccarthy|title=James J. McCarthy|website=Union of Concerned Scientists}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
* Distinguished Alumni Merit Award, Gonzaga University (1993)<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.gonzaga.edu/news-events/stories/2018/2/6/alumnus-james-mccarthy-receives-tyler-prize-for-environmental-achievement|title=Alumnus James McCarthy Receives Environmental Achievement Prize &#124; Gonzaga University|website=www.gonzaga.edu}}</ref>
* O’Leary Distinguished Scientist Lecture, Gonzaga University (2008)<ref name="auto"/>
* Walker Prize (2008)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2008/04/museum-of-science-to-honor-mccarthy-with-walker-prize/|title=Museum of Science to honor McCarthy with Walker Prize|date=April 3, 2008}}</ref>
* 2009 Scientist of the Year by the Harvard Foundation<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeb.harvard.edu/news/james-mccarthy-honored-scientist-year|title=James McCarthy Honored as Scientist of the Year|website=oeb.harvard.edu}}</ref>
*[[New England Aquarium]]’s David B. Stone Award<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://chge.hsph.harvard.edu/people/james-j-mccarthy |title=James J. McCarthy, Ph.D. &#124; Center for Health and the Global Environment |access-date=2018-04-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180403051715/https://chge.hsph.harvard.edu/people/james-j-mccarthy |archive-date=2018-04-03 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2018, James J. McCarthy was nominated as a recipient of the [[Tyler Prize for Environmental Achievement]] for his work on phytoplankton as it relates to climate change impacts and his outstanding leadership in the field of science policy. He shared the 2018 Tyler Prize, known as the "Nobel Prize" of the environment, with fellow biological oceanographer [[Paul Falkowski]] of Rutgers University.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://eos.org/articles/tyler-prize-honors-two-leaders-in-marine-and-climate-science|title=Tyler Prize Honors Two Leaders in Marine and Climate Science|website=Eos|date=7 February 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2018/02/harvards-james-mccarthy-honored-for-climate-change-insights/|title=Harvard's James McCarthy honored for climate change insights|date=February 28, 2018}}</ref>
